arithmetic: A SIMD lane owns one complete original K256 dot. Exact FP32 BF16 products, common original exponent, per-product truncation, unsigned modulo sum and original RZ bit normalization retain each K16 boundary. CPU/OS AVX512F/CD and ZMM state are checked before dispatch. Worker-local MXCSR establishes round-to-nearest and gradual underflow and is restored on exit. Unsupported operands or endpoints restart the complete original wide dot. No native BF16 dot-product approximation replaces canonical arithmetic.
comparison_scope: The initial executable compares current GPU prepared QK against16/32 CPU workers. The revision compares that GPU control and two32-worker CPU layouts, zero and16-float feature-row padding. Each candidate reads Q/K back from the actual run's GPU input tensors, prepares lossless key values/exponents, computes scores and uploads them; original one-wave probabilities, native PV and compact exact PV replay complete all variants. An independent original tiled QK pipeline supplies observer-only raw intermediates. Every original7169 context row matches external GB10; q8192 repeats1023 captured Q/K/V rows, comparing all33554432 outputs to original arithmetic, with external context for29364224 prefix cells. Every warmup and timed attempt checks scores, probabilities, scales, context, accumulators, denominators, error bounds, original candidate counts, checked guards and unused tails. Candidate index ordering is not a bytewise invariant. Golden data never enters computation.
timing_scope: One warmup and three rotated complete host-clock samples per128-query slab. CPU score time and blocking score-upload host time are included in the full attention clock and also reported separately. Actual input readback, CPU key encoding and worker construction/startup are charged once per candidate; GPU preparation belongs only to its control, and V transpose is common. Allocation, fixture reset, validation and immutable-input observers are outside clocks. No CPU/GPU overlap was implemented or measured. The retained GPU probability/native-PV/exact-PV stages are not separately profiled in this fixture. No hardware power, cache-event, occupancy or pipeline-speed inference is established; padding effects are observed elapsed-time comparisons.

decision.decision: Keep exact CPU QK and its corrected padded layout isolated. Feature-row padding materially lowers q8192 CPU score time in the paired executable but the32-worker padded producer alone remains slower than complete GPU attention. Full CPU replacement therefore has no performance case here. Partial CPU/GPU coexecution was not implemented or measured and is not ruled out universally; do not infer a pipeline speedup or transfer the component clocks to model TTFT. Continue a broader GPU arithmetic or dataflow route against the measured product wall.
